# Independent audit: signed shape compensation and the actual coupled roof

Audited `candidate 1d75b643f0e6e0cc` in full and Sections 5--7 of `candidate b85e6bd6eff40d13`, reading its Sections 1--4 for the exact construction and notation. **PASS.** One optional-corollary scope clarification was requested: the final invocation of the chord-gauge bound requires genuine depth attainment at y0 by the displayed caps, not merely equal budget and knowledge of the global maximum. The main signed-roof and signed-shape theorems do not need that extra condition.

## 1. The arbitrary-dimensional signed path

The root theorem explicitly assumes an actual compatible convex path, Hausdorff convergence, O(t) symmetric difference, its signed total-volume derivative, and a uniform cap first variation. It does not silently deduce those hypotheses for an arbitrary body deformation. Contracting B about any actual q in B preserves compatibility and changes its support exactly by -tv e_i, where e_i>=0.

A proper section of a convergent sequence of full-dimensional convex bodies converges after the parallel planes are identified, even when its height varies toward the limiting proper level. Upper inclusion follows by compactness. For lower inclusion, choose an interior point at the limiting section height and mix it with each point of the limiting section; these mixtures are interior, admit small balls, and eventually lie in the approximating bodies. A small adjustment in the normal coordinate then reaches the varying section height. Taking the mixture parameter to zero gives the claimed Hausdorff convergence. This also proves uniform section-volume convergence for heights in a shrinking interval, by the sequential characterization. The extra support displacement therefore has the stated -tv sigma_i e_i first variation, with its proper coarea normalization. Dimension one is immediate.

Hausdorff convergence leaves a fixed ball around y0 in all K_t. Its slices give a uniform lower slope bound for the scalar budgets; common bounding balls give a uniform upper bound. Symmetric differences and the support shift give uniform O(t) proximity to the old cap functions. The inverse-level sum therefore has one zero with O(t) changes in its common budget and levels. Continuity in the scalar budget for each t is enough; no unstated differentiability of the body path is required. The resulting source lies in the actual int K_t.

The given uniform first variations imply the finite linear equations for every subsequential derivative limit. Summing with the fixed proper-section weights cancels the one shared source motion and gives q_shape-vJ(q); spanning then fixes the full source derivative. Thus all the derivatives used by the theorem exist.

## 2. All sources and the tied endpoint payment

The moving middle traces cover the whole continuous space, including all newly added middle points. The ordinary A_t maximum is at most m_A plus the symmetric-difference volume, uniformly over all possible old and new points. Outside the original convex body the old depth is zero by separation; a boundary supporting cap also has zero d-volume. Its strict gap persists. Endpoint isolation by a finite integer tilt proves that the endpoint ordinary and mixed depths agree. The B maximum scales exactly as (1-vt)^d Q.

The true total mass derivative is D-dbv. The two normalized first-order numerators are exactly

    C+v(drb-J(q)),
    -r[D+dv(a+k)].

For D>0, v=0 is permitted by the second inequality; for D<=0 the permitted half-line begins strictly above v0=max(0,-D/[d(a+k)]). An affine function is negative somewhere on that half-line exactly when its slope is negative or its value at the lower endpoint is strictly negative. This proves the stated equivalence, including D=0 and equality boundary cases. When D<0, multiplying that boundary value by d(a+k) gives d(a+k)q_shape+D J(q)-dQD, with all signs correct.

The shape coefficients are fixed independently of the subsequently selected B contraction center. J is affine in that center, so its attained maximum is the displayed support-function expression with +h_B(-V). Both alternatives in the rate criterion are monotone in J. A single maximizing support point therefore suffices, including V=0. No independently optimal centers are combined.

## 3. Actual signed-roof compatibility

The polygonal roof construction retains all old K inequalities except its n-support inequality and replaces that inequality by the three actual inequalities (12). Their minimum profile is positive on I0, zero at its endpoints, and negative on the outer face excess. It therefore adds and removes real regions of K.

The face of D=(A+B)/2 is exactly I0. Each vertex outside that face has fixed negative normal height and satisfies all new roof inequalities for sufficiently small epsilon. The face points satisfy them because the profile is nonnegative on I0. The second seed (p+epsilon n+B)/2 has its F_B vertices exactly on the upper segment J; all other vertices have a strictly negative limiting height. All unchanged K facet inequalities hold for these seeds by the strict support argument for p in relint F_A. Minkowski addition distributes over convex hull, so these two finite seed checks prove compatibility for the whole (A_epsilon+B)/2.

The new inequalities have normals tending to n and bounded right sides; indeed one is exactly the old n normal with a small outward shift. Together with the unchanged facets they give uniform boundedness. Interior points of K eventually satisfy the new inequalities and every limit point satisfies the old ones, proving Hausdorff convergence. A fixed ball around y0 persists.

## 4. Boundary strips, signed areas, and menu motion

Away from the two face endpoints the other old facets have strict slack, and the roof boundary is exactly the prescribed three-piece profile. At an endpoint, the adjacent nonparallel facet meets each nearby roof line at a point displaced by O(epsilon); the relevant determinants stay nonzero. The corner correction therefore has width and height O(epsilon), hence area O(epsilon^2). Redundant collinear facets are explicitly removed. This is a valid polygonal argument and does not claim the same quadratic rate at general curved joins.

A proper original cut is either transverse to the face or has a positive parallel gap. In the transverse case, moving the cut by O(epsilon) changes the thin-strip contribution by O(epsilon^2); the parallel case is locally constant. Thus the signed cap coefficients in (15) are exact first-order terms uniformly near the source. Their signed added-minus-removed functions have vanishing Lipschitz constants in the source because their supporting bands have height O(epsilon). The inverse-map meeting point is actual and remains inside the moving K. Its menu covers every new middle point even though the path is not nested.

Inside I0, half the integral of G is L_A/8+L_B/4. The left outer contribution is -ell_L^2/(2d_L), because its ramp length is d_L/2; the right contribution is the analogous expression. Adding the A triangle area L_A/2 gives precisely

    D_s=5L_A/8+L_B/4-ell_L^2/(2d_L)-ell_R^2/(2d_R).

The largest possible coefficient follows from the two-term Cauchy inequality. With both excesses positive the stated ratio attains it. With a one-sided excess the supremum is approached as the corresponding denominator tends to L_A; if both are zero it is attained at every interior peak. The same actual peak must satisfy any simultaneous cost condition.

## 5. Ties and the optional outer-load condition

With strict gaps at both endpoints, the middle menu controls the new global upper certificate for small epsilon, even if its first derivative is negative. Thus C_s<0 suffices regardless of the signed mass change. If B is tied and unchanged, the first-order upper coefficient is max(q_s',0)-rD_s. It is strictly negative exactly when D_s>0 and C_s<0. This verifies both necessity and sufficiency for that stated first-order certificate, not for every conceivable variation.

On outer intervals, G<0. The explicitly assumed inequality W_K>=r therefore makes their signed cost nonpositive. Applying the already audited inner-trapezoid comparison gives (19) with the correct 5/4 and L_B/4 coefficients. This proves the stated sufficient repair. A low singleton load on an outer interval can reverse that contribution, and the source retains it.

The optional pair-load simplification uses the chord-gauge theorem only in a genuinely critical configuration at y0. Under that hypothesis its pair load is at least 1/4>r for r<2/9. Equal menu budgets alone do not prove the gauge premise; the author was asked to state this extra requirement explicitly. No automatic outer incidence, endpoint gap, favorable D_s, or favorable contraction-center payment is inferred by either audited theorem.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
